production.note: Calendar build years, German home market (the car was never sold new in the US: RM Sotheby's: "Furthermore, none of the 502 Evolution IIs produced were ever officially imported to the United States, which only heightens its exclusivity stateside."; rm-evo2). Mercedes-Benz Classic material reproduced by Sports Car Digest: "Mercedes produced just 502 units in 1990". Mercedes-Benz press release: "Within three months, a small series of 502 units was produced to obtain homologation for motor sport." (mb-press-evo2). Ultimate Specs (a database) gives "(1990 - 1991)" (ultimatespecs-evo2).

body.note: Four-door saloon (W201 190 E); inferred from the model.

displacementL.note: 2,463 cc per Encycarpedia (a database): "2,463 cc"; Ultimate Specs (a database): "150.3 cu-in / 2463 cm3" (ultimatespecs-evo2). Mercedes-Benz: "The 2.5 liter engine of the EVO II" (mb-press-evo2).

aspiration.note: Inferred: "2.5-liter 16-valve inline four-cylinder engine by Cosworth" with no forced induction.

drivetrain.note: Ultimate Specs (a database): "RWD". Rear-wheel drive like every W201.

transmission.note: RM Sotheby's (listing bullet): "five-speed Getrag manual transmission"; description: "Additionally, Getrag provided a five-speed "dogleg" gearbox to ensure fast and easy gear selection." Encycarpedia (a database): "Gearbox (MT)" "5 Gears" (encycarpedia-evo2).

powerHp.note: 235 PS (173 kW) converted (235 x 0.98632 = 231.8). Quote (Mercedes-Benz press release, Stuttgart, 8 February 2005, reproduced on GermanCarForum): "The 2.5 liter engine of the EVO II, as the car was known for short, developed an output of 235 hp (173 kW)"; Mercedes' English "235 hp" is the PS figure (173 kW = 232 hp). Mercedes-Benz Classic material reproduced by Sports Car Digest: "2.5-liter four-cylinder producing 235 hp at 7,200 rpm" (sportscardigest-evo2). Auto Bild (Matthias Techau): "235 PS leistet der 16-Ventil-Motor" (autobild-evo2). RM Sotheby's auction text prints "238-hp" (rm-evo2), not a manufacturer rating.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: two databases, agreeing; they may share an upstream source, so they may count as one. 1,340 kg converted (x 2.20462 = 2,954.2). Quote (Ultimate Specs, a database): "2954 lbs / 1340 kg" (Leergewicht). Encycarpedia (a database): "Kerb Weight" "1,340 kg" (encycarpedia-evo2). Mercedes-Benz's press release gives only a round figure: "The car, weighing some 1300 kilograms, accelerated from standstill to 100 km/h in just 7.1 seconds" (mb-press-evo2); see discrepancies. Standard car, 5-speed manual (the only transmission). Not stated whether DIN or EU.

discrepancies.reason: Mercedes-Benz's press release gives a round, approximate figure ("some 1300 kilograms"); the databases give a precise 1,340 kg.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 1,340 kg, the precise figure given by both databases; Mercedes' "some 1300" is an approximation, not a competing rating.

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 2,954 lb (1,340 kg) rests on Ultimate Specs and Encycarpedia (databases), agreeing but possibly drawing on the same upstream source; Mercedes' own press release says only "some 1300 kilograms". A Mercedes-Benz Classic technical-data sheet for the Evolution II (the public archive has one for the Evolution I, "Curb Weight: 1320 kg", but the Evolution II page could not be opened) or the Technische Daten page of auto motor und sport (https://www.auto-motor-und-sport.de/oldtimer/mercedes-190e-evo-ii-ellen-lohr-im-evo-baby-benz/technische-daten/, which refused the fetch under robots.txt), or an Evo or Autocar data panel, would replace it. Displacement in cc and drivetrain rest on databases.
